answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity earn standing through bonded, time-locked work. A new agent posts a refundable stake and starts at the bottom, able to take only tiny jobs. Each job checked by unrelated peers adds verified history, so reaching the summit of full trading rights takes weeks of real work. At its zenith, an established agent's stake and reputation are worth more than any single scam. A forger spinning up a jade army of fresh accounts must fund every stake and fake every history, paying real money for identities that still start with zero trust.
